evaluation_role: First and only claimed evaluation of previously unused internally generated synthetic seeds under a local frozen protocol. This is not externally supplied data, third-party preregistration, field evidence or a prospective physical experiment.
scope: Deployed observation assessment on 80 paired synthetic cases across two plant families, not independent field assets; executed-action checks are model-consistency tests.

protocol.training: First 70 healthy rows; fit eligibility checked before use. Otherwise defaults remain labelled assumptions. CUSUM bias uses the first 60 assumed-healthy minutes; instrument noise uses the first 60 samples. Post-gap windows are never relabelled as healthy commissioning.
protocol.targets: Separate reported hot-spot and observed-oil targets. True synthetic target errors are also reported for scoring only; no hidden temperatures enter assessment.
protocol.inputs: Observed voltage, loading, oil, reported hot-spot and ambient only in this fixed corpus. Optional phase observations are covered by separate consistency regressions, not independent phase-plant accuracy claims. No scenario, cooling, fault label, future row or true plant parameter.
protocol.limits: Two synthetic plant families, overlapping origins and paired seeds; these are not independent field assets. Event onset varies from minute 90 to 115. Primary MAE retains every eligible window including future disturbances. Disjoint timing partitions expose that distinction. Cases withheld for model discrepancy remain in coverage denominators. Combined-case diagnostic completion requires all expected signals concurrently. First and only claimed evaluation of previously unused internally generated synthetic seeds under a local frozen protocol. This is not externally supplied data, third-party preregistration, field evidence or a prospective physical experiment. Threshold-only uses per-channel observed limits and the same acquisition/domain gates, without residuals, CUSUM or forecasts; without-CUSUM is a separate ablation retaining residuals. No field validation, calibrated confidence or failure probability.
protocol.calibration_scope: Each synthetic case supplies 70 assumed-healthy rows for bounded oil identification and separately qualified winding-reference identification from reported hot-spot minus oil. Chronological validation gates both fits. A qualified winding reference changes conditional projections only; residual, channel-disagreement and CUSUM screening retain their configured reference. Oil-only mode never fits or applies winding calibration. Otherwise illustrative defaults remain. The observer gets past observations, never hidden cooling/fault settings. Scenario interventions remain separate internal consistency evidence.

comparison_contract.expected_signal_set: Matches the predefined EXPECTED signals while the synthetic disturbance is active; threshold-only cannot diagnose cooling or sensor-bias causes from a temperature limit.
comparison_contract.any_warning: Any valid observed threshold, acquisition/domain hold, model-disagreement signal, or qualified conditional limit forecast. Insufficient evidence alone is not counted as an alarm. Warning types are retained in the decision CSV.
comparison_contract.validity: Both assessors use the same available-channel and time/domain gates. Valid breaches on other channels remain visible during missing-data holds. Threshold checks need no residual warm-up and do not inherit model-disagreement holds.
comparison_contract.false_alarm: Any-warning false alarms are counted separately from historical diagnostic-only false alarms; labelled inactive synthetic minutes define the denominator.
comparison_contract.early_warning: Only warnings after event onset and before the true synthetic critical crossing qualify. A warning is not proof of correct cause or a safe operating deadline.

overall.note: Difference = baseline first warning minus full-pipeline first warning, among cases with a true synthetic critical crossing and both warning timestamps. Positive means full pipeline warned earlier. Missing timestamps remain explicit, not zero. First-warning categories can overlap. An earlier discrepancy warning is not necessarily a forecast-derived benefit.
